M2-T7.notes: DONE 2026-09-17: M2-T7 — the KIT TEST HARNESS, and the M2 machine gate as executable data. src/kit/harness/ (6 modules + tests): (1) renderTree.ts is the headless render model — jsdom has no WebGL, so instead of mounting a <Canvas> the harness WALKS the React element tree a module component returns and extracts one item per <mesh> (geometry, §4 slot, position, rotation). The walk resolves function components by CALLING them (the kit's render layer is hookless by construction) and rejects anything the kit's vocabulary does not allow: a stray host element, a mesh without exactly one geometry + one material, a cone where the kit draws uniform cylinders, a material with no slot name. It is node-loadable (no DOM) yet pinned against a REAL react-dom render of the same components (same mesh count, same geometry args, same slot names, same transforms) so the model can never silently drift from what React does. (2) components.ts = the standalone render surface (MODULE_COMPONENTS: one component per authored module + moduleComponentFor/moduleSceneElement); StandaloneModuleScene.tsx mounts exactly ONE module by id at a deck-local pose. (3) checks.ts = the four pure rule groups: slots (themeAssignsSlot per drawn slot — the M1-T4 rule asked per module, newly exported from src/materials/theme.ts so it is NEVER forked), render (rendered items vs the module's own parts 1:1), sockets (per-axis mm residuals against the contract kit's origin index; the pass/fail decision stays with M2-T2 moduleContractProblems), and the render-component lookup. (4) harness.ts = runModuleHarness / runKitHarness / assertKitHarnessClean — NEVER throws on the authored kit (problems are data, same posture as the M0-T6 harness and the M1-T3 validator), reporting per module: integrity, contract, slots, render, plus parts/meshes/slots/light+equipment anchors/door-socket residual rows, and kit-level rules (unique ids, every contract module authored so a spec ref resolves, a component for every module, the M1-T4 theme gate).
